title: Forward `PAGER` parameters to the temp-file pager and parse `less` flags
summary:
`_tempfilepager` now passes the parameters from `PAGER` to the pager, before the temporary file name. On Windows, `PAGER="less -R"` now runs `less -R` instead of bare `less`.

The PR also replaces the substring check for raw mode in `_pipepager`. The new `_less_uses_raw_mode` splits `LESS` and the pager arguments into tokens. Only short-option clusters with an `r`, and `--raw-control-chars`, count as a raw-mode request. This removes false positives from filenames such as `requirements.txt`. It also changes the result for a `LESS` value without a dash, such as `FRX`.

changes.what: Adds `_less_uses_raw_mode`, which splits `LESS` with `shlex.split` and checks each option token. `_pipepager` calls it and matches the pager by `cmd_path.stem`. `_tempfilepager` takes a new `cmd_params` argument and passes it to `subprocess.call`.
changes.why: Color detection for `less` no longer reacts to an `r` in filenames or long-option values. Windows users keep the options they set in `PAGER`. The detection now also ignores `LESS` values without a leading dash, which `less` accepts.

changes.what: Adds parametrized tests for `less` detection by file stem, case-insensitive matching on Windows, raw-mode token parsing, and parameter forwarding in the temp-file pager.
changes.why: The cases cover filenames with `r`, long options with values, `--`, and an unparsable `LESS`. They do not cover a dashless `LESS` such as `FRX`, or short options with attached values such as `-orecord.log`.

changes.what: Adds two entries to the unreleased section: parameter forwarding in the temp-file pager, and token-based raw-mode detection.
changes.why: Documents the user-visible pager behavior change.

flow.caption: `echo_via_pager` opens a pager through `_pager_contextmanager`, which picks `_tempfilepager` on Windows and `_pipepager` elsewhere. Both now receive the `PAGER` parameters. `_pipepager` asks `_less_uses_raw_mode` whether to keep colors.

risks.title: A dashless `LESS` value such as `FRX` no longer keeps colors
risks.reason: `_less_uses_raw_mode` reads only tokens that start with `-`, so `LESS=FRX` returns `False` at line 545. `less` accepts dashless option strings, and `FRX` is a common value (it is Git's default). Line 582 then skips the `LESS=-R` injection because `LESS` is set, and `get_pager_file` strips all ANSI styling. The old substring check found the `R` and kept colors.

risks.title: An `r` in an attached option value turns on colors
risks.reason: Line 542 treats any `r` after the first dash as a raw-mode flag. `less` options such as `-o`, `-k`, and `-P` take an attached value, so `LESS=-orecord.log` returns `True`. Click then keeps the ANSI codes, but `less` is not in raw mode and shows them as `ESC[` text.

risks.title: The Windows temp-file pager still drops colors
risks.reason: `_tempfilepager` yields `color` unchanged at line 657, so automatic detection stays `None`. `get_pager_file` treats `None` as no color and strips ANSI codes before they reach the file. `PAGER="less -R"` now reaches `less` at line 660, but styled output still shows plain unless the caller passes `color=True`.

tests.description: Run a Click command that calls `echo_via_pager` with styled text and `LESS=FRX`. Check whether colors still show; before this PR they did.
Set `LESS=-orecord.log`, page styled text, and confirm that `less` does not show raw `ESC[` sequences.
On Windows, set `PAGER="less -R"`, page styled text, and confirm that `less` receives `-R`. Then check whether the colors appear.
On Linux, set `PAGER="less -X"` with `LESS` unset. Confirm the pager starts with `-X` and that no `LESS=-R` is injected.
